proof:
# Actual opposite residual regions force a large missed intersection

Let d>=2 and m=d+1. Let v_0,...,v_d span R^d, with their sole
linear dependence sum_i v_i=0, and let

    T={x:v_i.x<=1 for all i}

be the corresponding bounded full-dimensional simplex. Let A,B,K be
d-dimensional convex bodies satisfying B subset T and (A+B)/2 subset K.
Write b=vol_d(B)>0. For each index j define the actual open residual
region

    R_j=A intersect intersection_(i!=j){x:v_i.x<-1}.

Suppose two distinct indices j,l satisfy

    vol_d(R_j)>0,          vol_d(R_l)>0.              (1)

Then the simultaneous missed region of the other d-1 middle traces
satisfies the exact strict bound

    vol_d(K intersect intersection_(i notin {j,l}){x:v_i.x<0})
                   > b/2^(d-1).                    (2)

No criticality, cap mass equality, or chosen center theorem is assumed.
The conclusion concerns one actual common subset of K.

## Proof

Choose actual points P in R_j and R in R_l. Because the normals sum
to zero, v_j.P>d, whereas v_j.R<-1. Thus their segment E=[P,R]
has longitudinal t=v_j.x span

    D=v_j.P-v_j.R>d+1=m.                            (3)

For every index i outside {j,l}, both endpoints have v_i-coordinate
strictly below -1. Convexity places the whole segment inside A and
strictly inside every one of those missed halfspaces. Since B subset T,

    (E+B)/2 subset
       K intersect intersection_(i notin {j,l}){x:v_i.x<0}. (4)

It remains to bound the volume of this one swept convex set. Let e be
the direction of E normalized by v_j.e=1. Use coordinates x=y+t e,
y in ker(v_j), with transverse measure

    dnu(y)=dH_(d-1)(y)/||v_j||.

The Jacobian is exact: the component of e perpendicular to ker(v_j)
is1/||v_j||. Let P_B be the nu-measure of B's transverse projection.
This measure is finite and positive because B is a convex body.
Each nonempty section of E+B is obtained from the corresponding B
interval by adding an interval of t-length D. Fubini gives

    vol_d(E+B)=b+D P_B.                              (5)

The coordinate t ranges over [-d,1] on T. The lower bound follows
from v_j.x=-sum_(i!=j)v_i.x>=-d; its range has length m. Every B
section therefore has t-length at most m, and another use of Fubini
gives b<=m P_B. Equations(3)--(5) imply

    vol_d(E+B)>b+m P_B>=2b.

Finally the midpoint dilation in(4) multiplies d-volume by2^(-d).
This proves(2), including its strictness.

The same argument retains any quantified span: if particular actual
P in R_j,R in R_l have t-span D, then the left side of(2) is at least

    2^(-d)[b+D P_B] >=2^(-d)(1+D/m)b.              (6)

## Scope and the planar consequence

The positivity assumptions in(1) may be verified by inclusion-exclusion
from actual cap areas, but the lemma itself does not replace them by
independent marginal data. The residual regions are open only to make
the strict missed inequalities transparent; their finitely many boundary
hyperplanes have zero d-volume. The set in(4) is one swept set, so there
is no summation over overlapping inclusions.

For d=2 its conclusion is a single missed middle cap of area>b/2.
In the genuinely critical three-fiber regime, the separate exact
profiles and the additive captured reserve turn this into a<b/9 under
a-u-w>0. The complete planar derivation is Section6 of
`candidate 6b20e938071f0379`.
No higher-dimensional depth conclusion is inferred from(2).
